name: Treaty with the Appalachicola Band, 1832 (Blunt and Davy)
aka: Agreement of Tallahassee, October 11, 1832, with John Blunt and O Saa Hajo (Davy)
nations: Apalachicola towns of John Blunt and Davy (Tuski Hajo's town), Florida
promises: Article 1: the chiefs gave up the four-mile reserve on the Apalachicola made for them by the additional article of the Treaty of Camp Moultrie (1823) and agreed to remove their 256 people west of the Mississippi.
Article 2: $13,000 for the surrender and to cover exploring, emigration and subsistence: $3,000 in cash at signing and $10,000 when the whole party began to remove.
Article 3: the reserve to be left by November 1, 1833, with up to one more year allowed if unavoidable circumstances delayed it.
Article 4: Blunt and Davy's share of the $5,000 Camp Moultrie annuity continued while they stayed in Florida, and the balance of the annuity term advanced when they removed.
today: No court, Indian Claims Commission or government finding about this agreement was found. The Seminole land claim before the Indian Claims Commission (Docket 73) concerned the Seminole cessions in Florida; the parts of it opened did not deal with this band's reserve or payments.

openQuestions: Whether the $10,000 under Article 2 and the advanced annuity under Article 4 were paid when the band removed was not traced; Indian Office removal accounts would settle it.
Secondary sources say Blunt's band went to Texas rather than to the Creek country; this was not confirmed from a primary record and is left out.
treaties.json names the Muscogee (Creek) Nation as the present-day nation; no nation account of this agreement was found, and which nations descend from Blunt's band was not settled.
